observation.visible_scene: Low-angle shot of a single leek lying flat on gray asphalt, its frayed root end at the left and its leafy green end at the right, positioned under the dark undercarriage of a car. The car's right tire sits to the right of the leek, initially with a small gap between the tread and the leafy end.
visible_changes: The tire rolls slowly leftward from the start of the excerpt; the gap between the tire and the leafy end narrows over roughly the first 0.5 s.
Around 1.0–1.4 s the tire reaches and begins to flatten the leafy green end of the leek.
From about 1.4 s to 2.4 s the tire keeps rolling left, pinning and flattening the white stalk progressively from the leaf end toward the root end.

By ~2.4–2.7 s the tire is over the root end; the stalk is largely hidden beneath it and only the frayed root tuft remains briefly visible at the lower-left edge of the tire before being mostly occluded.
A small green leaf fragment is pushed out to the right of the tire and stays on the asphalt in the later frames.
The leek's root end stays essentially fixed on the ground until the tire arrives, showing the leek is stationary while the tire moves over it.

The framing changes across the clip: the upper bumper/undercarriage and the bright background road strip move out of view while the tire grows larger in frame, indicating camera movement (a closer, lower viewpoint on the wheel) alongside the car's rolling.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the car was already in motion before this segment or whether it stops after the root end passes under the tire.
The final state of the leek after the tire has fully rolled over it.
Any action of the car's other wheels or what lies to the left outside the crop.
uncertain_details: The precise division between camera motion and car motion that makes the tire appear to grow and the background shift cannot be fully separated from the frames alone.
Exact contact and crush timings are approximate given the sampling interval.
